title: How much money for a comfortable retirement
subtitle: Setting a retirement savings target in VND
openingQuestion: Linh estimates her monthly living costs in retirement (in today's prices) at about 15 million VND, or 180 million VND/year. Using the simple rule of thumb 'you need about 25 times annual spending', roughly how much does Linh need to accumulate to live off her investment portfolio (not counting her BHXH pension)?
openingOptions: It can't be estimated at all, since spending always changes
explanation: The '25 times annual spending' rule comes from the idea of withdrawing about 4%/year from a portfolio without running out of money too fast. With spending of 180 million/year, the reference savings target is 180 million x 25 = 4.5 billion VND. This figure does NOT include the BHXH pension, and needs adjusting for inflation since it's estimated in today's terms.

realWorldExample.company: Estimating retirement costs for urban workers in Vietnam
realWorldExample.description: Based on cost-of-living surveys in major cities like Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, a retired household (no longer raising children, no home loan left) typically needs about 10-20 million VND/month to maintain a stable standard of living, depending on region and lifestyle, not counting medical costs, which tend to rise with age. This gives each person a basis for estimating a savings target suited to their own circumstances, rather than applying one number to everyone.

quiz.question: What is the '25 times annual spending' rule used for?
options: Estimating the total amount needed to retire
Estimating the number of years you need to keep working before retiring
Calculating the maximum amount that can be withdrawn from the fund each month
Calculating the monthly BHXH pension you'll receive
quiz.explanation: The 25-times rule comes from the inverse of a 4%/year withdrawal rate (100/4 = 25) - a rate some studies suggest can be sustained for decades, though it should be applied cautiously in Vietnam given different inflation dynamics.

quiz.question: When calculating a retirement savings target in Vietnam, why should you SUBTRACT the expected BHXH pension before applying the 25-times rule?
options: Because the 25-times rule only applies to foreign markets
Because BHXH already covers part of your monthly spending
Because the BHXH pension isn't subject to personal income tax
Because the BHXH pension always rises faster than inflation
quiz.explanation: If expected annual spending is 180 million and the BHXH pension is estimated to cover 60 million/year, the amount your personal portfolio has to cover is only 120 million/year, so the reference savings target drops to about 120 million x 25 = 3 billion VND instead of 4.5 billion VND.

quiz.question: Spending is 200 million/year, and the estimated BHXH pension is 60 million/year. What is the reference savings target?
options: 1.5 billion VND, taking the 60 million pension times 25
5 billion VND, taking the entire 200 million spending times 25
3.5 billion VND, taking the 140 million difference times 25
It can't be calculated without knowing the person's expected lifespan
quiz.explanation: Only the portion of spending the portfolio has to carry gets multiplied by 25: (200 - 60) x 25 = 3.5 billion. Ignoring the pension sets a target roughly one and a half billion higher than reality is - enough to discourage plenty of people out of planning altogether.

quiz.question: What does the 4%-per-year withdrawal rule assume?
options: The retiree will live exactly twenty-five more years
All the money gets moved into a savings deposit right at retirement
Inflation is zero throughout the person's retirement
The portfolio keeps being invested and earning a return after retirement
quiz.explanation: The 4% figure assumes the portfolio stays invested in the market and keeps growing - if it's all moved into a savings deposit, the safe withdrawal rate is much lower. This is why the advice to 'sell all your stocks once you retire' usually backfires.

quiz.question: Why adjust expected spending for inflation when calculating the target?
options: Because 200 million today will buy far less twenty years from now
Because the tax authority requires everything to be converted to future value
Because inflation raises the BHXH pension faster than spending
Because the 25-times rule is only correct when inflation stays exactly at 4%
quiz.explanation: At 4% annual inflation, the standard of living equivalent to 200 million today would cost about 440 million after 20 years. Calculating the target at today's prices and leaving it unchanged is the most common way a retirement plan ends up half-funded.

quiz.question: Which expense is most commonly underestimated in a retirement plan?
options: Food, since food prices rise faster than every other category
Medical costs, since they rise quickly with age and are hard to predict
Transportation, since retirees travel more than they did while working
Housing, since rents always rise faster than retirement income
quiz.explanation: Many expenses fall in retirement - commuting, work clothes, raising children. Medical costs go the other way, and they're the one category that can hit with a single very large expense. This is why health insurance and a separate medical reserve fund aren't optional extras.

keyTakeaways: Quick estimate: reference savings target = (expected annual retirement spending - estimated BHXH pension) x 25
Calculate spending in today's terms, then adjust for expected inflation up to the retirement year
Medical costs tend to rise with age, so add a separate medical reserve on top
This is only a starting reference figure - review and adjust it periodically as income, spending, and actual life goals change

practicePrompt.question: Hung expects to spend 20 million/month in retirement (240 million/year), and estimates a BHXH pension of 8 million/month (96 million/year). Applying the 25-times rule, how much does he need to accumulate from his personal investment portfolio?
options: About 3.6 billion VND = (240 million - 96 million) x 25, since the BHXH pension already covers part of it
About 6 billion VND, calculated as the full 240 million x 25, since there's no need to subtract the BHXH pension when applying this rule
About 2.4 billion VND, calculated as 96 million x 25, since only the expected BHXH pension itself needs to be calculated
It can't be calculated without knowing Hung's exact statutory retirement age
practicePrompt.explanation: (240 million - 96 million) x 25 = 144 million x 25 = 3.6 billion VND. You need to subtract the portion BHXH already covers before multiplying by 25, since that part of spending is already handled by another source.

summary.keyIdea: Quick estimate: reference savings target = (expected annual retirement spending - estimated BHXH pension) x 25
summary.commonMistake: Reading the concept as a phrase to memorize rather than a principle to apply to a real decision.
summary.action: Calculate spending in today's terms, then adjust for expected inflation up to the retirement year

application.title: Estimate your own retirement target
application.message: Estimate the annual spending you want in retirement, subtract your expected BHXH pension, then multiply by 25 to get a reference savings target for yourself.
application.secondary: This is only a starting point - review it periodically as your income and goals change.

sections.text: 'How much money is enough to retire?' is the question that makes a lot of people put off planning altogether, because the number feels either too huge or too vague. There's actually a fairly simple way to start estimating it.

The first step is to estimate monthly living costs in retirement, in today's terms (not yet adjusted for inflation). For a family in a large Vietnamese city, a reasonable retirement spending level (no more children to raise, no home loan left) typically runs 10-20 million VND/month depending on lifestyle and location.

A common way to estimate is to multiply expected annual spending by 25, based on the assumption that you can withdraw about 4% of the portfolio's value each year without running out of money too fast (the next lesson explains this 4% rule in detail). For example, spending 15 million/month, or 180 million/year, gives a reference savings target of 180 million x 25 = 4.5 billion VND.

items: Step 1: estimate monthly spending in retirement at today's prices (food, housing, transportation, medical care, leisure)
Step 2: multiply by 12 to get annual spending
Step 3: estimate the expected annual BHXH pension (based on average contribution salary and years of participation)
Step 4: subtract the expected BHXH pension from annual spending to get the portion your personal portfolio has to cover
Step 5: multiply that portion by 25 to get a reference savings target (in today's terms)

sections.label: Don't forget to adjust for inflation
sections.text: The figure above is in today's terms. If you're still 25 years from retirement and inflation averages 3.5%/year, actual living costs at that point will be considerably higher than today - 180 million VND/year today could equal more than 420 million VND/year after 25 years at 3.5% inflation. The savings target needs to be scaled up accordingly, not left as the figure calculated at today's prices.
A factor often overlooked: medical costs

Medical costs tend to rise quickly with age and usually rise faster than general inflation. When estimating retirement spending, it's worth setting aside a separate medical reserve (you can reference supplementary health insurance costs and routine checkups) instead of lumping it into regular living expenses, to avoid underestimating actual needs at an older age.

lines: The 25-times-spending rule is a useful starting point, not an absolute number - adjust it for inflation, your expected BHXH pension, and your own medical costs.
Knowing a specific target figure, even as an estimate, makes it far easier to set a realistic monthly savings and investment plan than a vague 'save as much as possible'.
